news.title: Morocco Could Welcome the World’s Biggest Clubs in 2029
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco has emerged as a strong contender to host the 2029 FIFA Club World Cup amid ongoing discussions between FIFA and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) over the scheduling and organization of major international and continental competitions. According to reports, recent developments in discussions surrounding the future organization of the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) could improve Morocco's chances of hosting the global club competition. If confirmed, the tournament would take place just one year before Morocco co-hosts the 2030 FIFA World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal. Morocco's potential bid is supported by its growing sports infrastructure, including stadium modernization projects, hotel facilities, and logistical capabilities.

news.title: Men's World Cup: Mexico's most creative football pitches
news.lede: On the southern outskirts of Mexico City, amateur teams meet on a very unique football pitch every Sunday. Known as the "Field of the Gods," it is perched inside the extinct Teoca volcano and situated a breathtaking 2,700 meters (8,800 feet) above sea level. The pitch was created by the nearby community more than 60 years ago and is a source of local pride. Cars above, sports below: this pitch in Mexico City's colorful Las Aguilas neighborhood gives people the space to play soccer beneath a highway overpass.

news.title: Player ratings: Off-contract gun has ‘made Test football look easy’
news.lede: Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters has had three games to get a thorough look at his players before the World Cup finals. In game one, the Aussies pipped New Zealand 24-22, then came a 36-22 win over Fiji, and on Saturday night a 66-6 thumping of the Cook Islands. Jack Bostock celebrates a try with Latrell Mitchell. Now that the Kangaroos’ pool-round games are in the books, I have rated every Aussie player out of 10.

news.title: Zambrotta unusual surgery for Italy’s 2006 World Cup winner
news.lede: Italy’s World Cup winner Gianluca Zambrotta was well known for being bow-legged, but reveals they had become so painful that he had experimental surgery to correct them. The 49-year-old was one of the key figures in Italy’s 2006 World Cup triumph, as well as amassing silverware playing for Juventus, Barcelona and Milan. His unusual gait and running style were in part because he was bow-legged, but what had seemed to be an advantage in his playing career brought much bigger problems off the field. Zambrotta revealed he had two operations to straighten out his legs, hoping this will reduce the pain that he said was becoming unsustainable, making even going up and down stairs extremely difficult.
